Expects a positive decimal string such as "0.000131" (scientific notation is not parsed). referencePrice.description: Requester-provided price (output units per input unit, human units) to compare router quotes against. When fastestInPriceRange is enabled for the API key, destination-leg quotes more than 20% below it are skipped. When useRouteRacingOnOrigin is set, it anchors origin swap route selection: routes priced within a fixed band of it (20% below to 50% above) are preferred, and the best route overall is used when none is in the band. The selected route alone sets the expected and minimum output (with slippageTolerance applied to it); the reference price never sets a floor. Expects a positive decimal string such as "0.000131" (scientific notation is not parsed). Deliberately unconstrained by a schema pattern: a malformed or non-positive value, or one sent by a key without the relevant grant, is ignored and the quote is served without a reference price rather than rejected.

useRouteRacing.description: Whether to use route racing for this quote (executing multiple candidate routes on-chain and keeping the best), when the API key is authorized for it.

useRouteRacingOnOrigin.description: Whether to use route racing for this quote's origin swap (executing multiple candidate routes on-chain and keeping the best), when the API key is authorized for it and the origin chain is configured for route racing.

ttl.description: Time-to-live for the quote, in seconds, measured from when the quote was generated. If the request is not filled within this window it is refunded instead of filled.

useQueueing.description: Opt-in queueing: when the destination fill hits temporarily insufficient liquidity, keep retrying it until the queueingTtl window expires (then refund) instead of refunding immediately. Requires queueingTtl.

queueingTtl.description: Queueing window, in seconds, measured from when the quote was generated. While it is open, a useQueueing request that hits insufficient destination liquidity is retried instead of refunded; once it expires the request is refunded. Independent of ttl. Only used together with useQueueing.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: JSON-encoded array of filter-group objects. Fields within each group are AND'd; groups are OR'd. Prefix a key with 'not:' to negate it (must_not). Values can be a scalar or an array (OR semantics within the field). Example: [{"depositAddress":"0xabc","originChainId":8453},{"depositAddress":"0x123","originChainId":1}]. Negation example: [{"not:status":"failure"}]. Array value example: [{"not:status":["failure","refund"]}]. A value of null is a null-check ("is empty"/"is not empty") instead of an equality test, for any key. Null-check example: [{"depositAddress":null}] (is empty / does not exist), [{"not:depositAddress":null}] (is not empty / exists). null cannot be combined with real values in an array. At most 50 distinct string values across id, term, and grouped id/term filters (including negations) are allowed; a top-level id with includeChildRequests is excluded from this limit. Requests are limited to the caller’s integrator and requests without an API key. A `referrer` key (or `not:referrer`) without top-level `apiKeyId` or `apiKey` limits that group to public keyless requests. Optional key parameters must contain keys owned by the authenticating integrator. Referrer groups also include matching public keyless requests regardless of age; groups without a referrer retain their existing scope unless a top-level referrer is supplied.
